newsitem.title: GERMANY: 10 German states invite bids for 2nd pooled bond.
newsitem.headline: 10 German states invite bids for 2nd pooled bond.

text.p: Ten German federal states plan to issue a joint "Jumbo" bond with a coupon of six percent and a volume of 4.5 billion marks, the finance ministry of the state of Hesse said on Wednesday.
Bids for the bond are due by 1000 GMT on Thursday, January 16, the ministry said in a statement.
The bond is the second pooled "Laender" bond to be issued by a group of German federal states.
Seven of Germany's 16 states, or Laender, launched a joint four billion mark, 10-year Jumbo bond last August in the first pooled state debt issue of its kind.
The new bond matures on January 29, 2007. It will be placed via a consortium of market-making banks.

The consortium must consist of at least three and at most six banks which are experienced in placing large volume debt issues and undertaking the necessary market-smoothing activities, the ministry said.
Bids must be based on a yield spread to the benchmark 10-year federal government Bund issue which has a coupon of six percent and matures on January 4, 2007, the statement said.
The issuing states are North Rhine-Westphalia, Berlin, Hamburg, Hesse, Rhineland-Palatinate, Schleswig-Holstein, Brandenburg, Bremen, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and Saarland.
North Rhine-Westphalia is liable for the largest portion of the issue with one billion marks. Four states have portions of 250 million marks and five have shares of 500 million marks.
The bond has the securities number 113502.
